text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

JOSEPH GUILLOTIN, French physician and advocate of humane capital punishment, was born in 1738. The first execution using the decapitation machine that would later bear his name took place on April 25, 1792. Contrary to myth, he did not die on the guillotine and the Guillotin family made strenuous but futile efforts to have the machine called something else.

Britain's youngest ever Prime Minister WILLIAM PITT (The Younger) was born in 1759. He became Prime Minister at the age of 24 in 1783, holding office until 1801 and returning to the post in 1804 during the Napoleonic wars.
Brewer ROBERT TOOTH was born in 1821. He founded the Kent brewery in Sydney as a Protestant competitor for the Catholic owned Tooheys brewery.
Australian merchant SIR CHARLES LLOYD-JONES was born in 1878. He became a director of Sydney radio station 2BL, and eventually was the first Chairman of the ABC.

British author IAN FLEMING was born in 1908. After a career in Naval intelligence, he wrote the novel 'Casino Royale' on the night before his wedding. That novel gave birth to fiction's greatest spy JAMES BOND.
Australian author PATRICK WHITE was born in 1912. He became famous for his novels including "Happy Valley", "The Tree of Man" and "Voss". WHITE won the Nobel Prize for literature in 1973.
Labor politician TOM UREN was born in 1921. He became famous for his stance against the Vietnam War.

US singer GLADYS KNIGHT was born in 1944. She formed the family-based 'GLADYS KNIGHT and The Pips' in 1952. Their hits included "Every Beat Of My Heart" (1961), "I Heard It Through The Grapevine" (1967), "Midnight Train To Georgia" (1973), "Best Thing That Ever Happened To Me" (1974), "On And On" (1974), "Love Overboard" (1988) and "Licence To Kill" (1989).

Australian singer and former soapie star KYLIE MINOGUE was born in 1968. She made her name on the soap opera 'Neighbours' before switching to a singing career. Her first hit in Australia was a cover version of "Locomotion" (1988). Other hits
included "I Should Be So Lucky" (1988), "Got To Be Certain" (1988), "Hand On You Heart" (1989) and "Never Too Late" (1989).
** EVENTS **
1873 : Rough weather wrecked 143 ships off the coast of
England in the one day.
1891 : The world's first weightlifting championship was
held at the Cafe Monico in London.
1901 : WILLIAM KNOX D'ARCY was granted a concession to
explore for oil. He founded British Petroleum.
1937 : The famous Austrian psychiatrist ALFRED ADLER died
in Vienna. He introduced the concept of the 'inferiority complex'.
1940 : The Belgian Army surrendered to the Germans in
World War Two.
1940 : Norwegian and British forces captured Narvik in
Norway.
1940 : Evacuation of the defeated Allied armies from
Dunkirk began. By its completion on the night of June 2, a total of 224,585 British and 112,546 French and Belgian troops had been saved.
1958 : The US government approved statehood for Alaska.
1965 : The British round-the-world solo yachtsman SIR
FRANCIS CHICHESTER was given a hero's welcome as he arrived home from his epic 119-day journey.
1969 : The relatives of NED KELLY were among those who
protested against the casting of pop singer MICK JAGGER as the infamous Australian bushranger.
1972 : The Duke of Windsor, who gave up the British
throne to marry American divorcee WALLIS SIMPSON, died in Paris.
1978 : Australia FRED SCHEPISI's "Chant of Jimmy
Blacksmith" received good reviews at the Cannes film festival.
1981 : Cardinal STEFAN WYSZYNSKI, Poland's Catholic
Primate and staunch oppoent of Warsaw's communist authorities, died.
1982 : In the Falklands war, British troops recaptured
Port Darwin and Goose Green from the Argentine army, taking at least 1,400 prisoners.
1982 : The Barcelona soccer club bought Argentine star
DIEGO MARADONA for a record nine-and-a-half million dollars.
1986 : Broadcaster DERRYN HINCH was sentenced to six
weeks jail and fined 25,000 dollars for contempt of court. The offences related to three broadcasts concerning a Catholic priest facing sex charges. Mr JUSTICE PETER MURPHY convicted
HINCH warning him against trial by media. HINCH who had pleaded not guilty, unsuccessfully appealed to the High Court. He served 28 days in jail in 1987.
1987 : West German teenager MATHIAS RUST landed his

Cessna light plane in Moscow's Red Square. The incident caused major problems in the Soviet military because RUST had managed to fly from HELSINKI to MOSCOW without being spotted on radar. MIKHAIL GORBACHEV used the incident to purge the Soviet military of many hardline generals.
1990 : The yacht 'Maiden' created history in the
Whitbread Round the World yacht race, by becoming the first yacht to finish with an all-female crew.
1990 : Australian lawyers STEPHEN MELROSE and NICK SPANOS
were gunned down by the IRA in Holland. They had been mistaken for off-duty British soldiers.
1991 : In Ethiopia, rebel tanks blasted their way into
Addis Ababa at dawn, toppling the remnants of a Marxist government whose 17-year rule brought war and famine.
1995 : Russia's worst recorded earthquake killed 1,989
people in the Far East oil-producing town of Neftegorsk, on the north of Sakhalin Island. The quake measured 7.5 on the Richter scale.
1996 - President JACQUES CHIRAC announced France would end military conscription from 1997, earlier than previously planned.
